analysis.title: Fed Holds Rates Steady: A Matter of Time
key_insights: The FOMC held the federal funds target range at 3.75-4.00% on 10/28/2026. Markets price a hike in December followed by three more increases in 2027.
Headline CPI reaccelerated to 3.74% y/y in September, from 3.40% in August and 3.36% in July. WTI crude is trading well above $100 per barrel, adding to inflation pressure.

Core PCE may offer little relief near term because of unfavorable base effects. Allspring expects those effects to reverse meaningfully in the first half of 2027, which could shift the balance of risks.

Growth signals are mixed. The Atlanta Fed GDP tracker shows 3.3% annualized Q3 growth, October manufacturing PMI rose to 54.5, and September retail sales rose 6.3% y/y (not adjusted for inflation). September nonfarm payrolls rose only 29,000 versus 133,000 in August, with signs of wage disinflation.

Allspring says the market pricing of strong growth plus sticky inflation is not its base case. OIS pricing implies three hikes next year, yet the probability of rates falling over 12 months has also risen, which Allspring reads as an unusually wide distribution of outcomes. The rate path could reprice if growth disappoints or inflation eases.
AI capital expenditure supports near-term demand and could raise productivity over the long term. Supply constraints could delay the productivity benefit while the investment impulse continues.

Core PCE and GDP estimates are due the day after the Fed meeting, ahead of the U.S. midterm elections. Markets are also watching the Fed's view of the AI buildout, its balance sheet and global sovereign bond moves.

Fixed income: real yields are becoming attractive, but Allspring sees little catalyst for nominal yields to fall absent a growth shock or risk-off event. It favors the intermediate part of the U.S. curve and is cautious on longer-duration government bonds. Outside the U.S., repricing creates better entry points where policy expectations look overly hawkish.
Equities: constructive despite higher real yields, favoring broad-based U.S. exposure with selectivity toward quality and sentiment.

Currencies: the U.S. dollar is seen as a strong portfolio diversifier and attractive versus select developed market currencies. Allspring is cautious on the euro and selectively positive on emerging market currencies.

macro_indicators.reading: One hike in December, three further hikes in 2027
macro_indicators.interpretation: Markets price tightening. Allspring says this is not its base case.
Reaccelerated from 3.40% in August and 3.36% in July, reinforcing persistent inflation concerns.
Adds near-term inflation pressure from supply-driven input costs.
Points to resilient growth. This is a model-based nowcast, not an official print.
Strong, but not adjusted for inflation.
Down from 133,000 in August, a sign of labor market softening alongside wage disinflation.

trade_ideas.description: Favor the intermediate part of the U.S. Treasury curve and stay cautious on longer-duration government bonds
trade_ideas.rationale: Real yields are becoming attractive, but there is little catalyst for nominal yields to fall absent a growth shock or risk-off event.

trade_ideas.description: Long broad-based U.S. equity exposure with a quality and sentiment tilt
trade_ideas.rationale: Allspring is constructive on equities despite higher real yields.
trade_ideas.risk: Slowing growth, persistent inflation and geopolitical uncertainty argue for selectivity.

trade_ideas.description: Long U.S. dollar versus select developed market currencies, cautious on the euro, selectively long emerging market currencies
trade_ideas.rationale: The dollar is a portfolio diversifier, and weaker growth offsets the euro's repricing toward higher rates. EM currencies are supported by stronger growth, lower inflation and orthodox policy.

risk_factors: Growth disappoints and the market-implied hiking path reprices lower.
Supply-driven inflation from oil well above $100 per barrel complicates the Fed's assessment.
Softer payroll growth and wage disinflation could challenge the resilient activity picture.
Supply constraints could delay AI productivity gains while capex keeps adding demand.
Geopolitical uncertainty and slowing global growth.
vol_and_positioning: Allspring says differences in underlying economic conditions may contribute to higher financial market volatility.
OIS pricing implies three hikes next year while the probability of rate cuts over 12 months has also increased, which Allspring reads as an unusually wide distribution of outcomes.
geopolitical: Geopolitical uncertainty is cited as a reason for selectivity in equities.
U.S. midterm elections follow the concentrated set of macro catalysts.

tension_points.bull_case: Markets price a December hike and three more in 2027 on persistent inflation, oil above $100 and resilient activity (Atlanta Fed GDP tracker 3.3%, PMI 54.5).
tension_points.bear_case: Allspring says strong growth with sticky inflation is not its base case. Payrolls slowed to 29,000, wage disinflation is emerging, and base effects should reverse in the first half of 2027.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Growth disappoints or inflation begins to ease, which would reprice the expected rate path.

theme_stances.key_argument: Pricing implies strong growth with sticky inflation, which is not Allspring's base case, and the path is susceptible to repricing.
theme_stances.evidence: That is not our base case.

theme_stances.key_argument: Real yields are attractive, but there is little catalyst for nominal yields to fall, so the intermediate part of the curve is favored over longer duration.
theme_stances.evidence: continue to favor the intermediate part of the U.S. curve
